agent.name: Emerging Technology Diffusion Agent
agent.specialty: Rogers diffusion analysis and contextual timing

analytical_question: How far has generative AI and this human-reviewed service application diffused, and what does the evidence imply for this hypothetical organization over six months?
general_et_finding: US evidence indicates broad but uneven generative-AI diffusion beyond a small experimental niche. The August 2026 RPS tracker reports workplace use by 40.5% of employed adults; this is not a company deployment rate. Task-level research indicates uneven depth. A precise Rogers stage is not established: innovators and early adopters are insufficient as a description of all users, but early-majority participation is a plausible interpretation rather than a verified stage. Late majority and laggard shares cannot be assigned. Organizational posture cannot alter this general evidence.
application_finding: Human-reviewed routine banking replies have no directly measured adoption prevalence in the supplied packet. Finance/insurance use of any AI is not a bank service-drafting rate. Relative advantage: support-worker research suggests a possibility, not demonstrated bank value. Compatibility: sensitive information and internal approvals may complicate fit under the case assumptions. Complexity: verification and escalation require skills; training burden is unknown. Trialability: approved generic inquiries with no live customer data offer a bounded evaluation route, an inference. Observability: track correctness, escalation, total handling effort and data-handling exceptions, not speed alone. Potential accelerators are trusted internal demonstrations and reusable approved content; inhibitors are review effort and uncertainty about data handling. Service supervisors and internal control owners are candidate change agents, not verified industry opinion leaders. Approved content, access controls and staff training are complementary assets. No supplied evidence identifies a decisive standard or bank-specific diffusion stage; all five adopter categories remain unquantified.
organization_specific_finding: The hypothetical bank is conservative by assumption; this is not evidence that banks are late adopters. Its broad sector AI use can coexist with caution about this application. Within the six-month horizon, prioritize a controlled evaluation of approved generic content and internal review readiness before customer-data use. Its actual peer position is unknown.

evidence.claim: Broad-sector AI use: finance/insurance 33.9%, retail about 14%, as of May 3, 2026.
evidence.source_or_reference: US Census Bureau, Large Firms With at Least 20 Employees Biggest AI Users, https://www.census.gov/library/stories/2026/05/ai-use-businesses.html
evidence.notes: Any AI/business function, not generative AI customer-service adoption. Broad sectors differ from banks and apparel ecommerce. Historical context, not current October prevalence.

evidence.claim: August 2026 tracker reports workplace generative-AI use by 40.5% of employed adults.
evidence.source_or_reference: Harvard Project on Workforce and St. Louis Fed, Generative AI Adoption Tracker, https://pw.hks.harvard.edu/post/the-generative-ai-adoption-tracker
evidence.date_or_recency: Page initially published 2025-11-14, live updated; August 2026 observation; reviewed 2026-10-28
evidence.notes: Nationally weighted US RPS; self-reported individual use, not enterprise deployment. Dynamic page; exact update date unavailable. Do not equate workers with firms.

evidence.claim: Research using nearly 14,000 workers across August 2025-May 2026 finds broad but uneven task penetration.
evidence.source_or_reference: Bick et al., What Work Does Generative AI Do?, https://www.stlouisfed.org/on-the-economy/2026/sep/what-work-does-generative-ai-do
evidence.evidence_type: Research authors summarizing RPS task study
evidence.notes: US adults 18-64. Task and occupation denominators differ. Its May workplace headline differs from the August tracker observation; do not claim uninterrupted growth or merge waves without checking comparability.

evidence.claim: Revised study of 5,172 customer-support agents reports average 15% higher issues resolved per hour with AI assistance, with heterogeneous effects.
evidence.source_or_reference: Brynjolfsson, Li and Raymond, Generative AI at Work, https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.11771v2
evidence.evidence_type: Authors original research abstract, revised version
evidence.notes: Historical effectiveness evidence, not a market-prevalence estimate or guaranteed savings. Experienced/high-skilled workers had small quality declines. Full methods and underlying observation dates not yet checked. Do not mix with earlier 14%/5,179 version.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: No representative application-specific prevalence or pilot-versus-production split for the target peer groups.
The effect study shows heterogeneous outcomes and some quality deterioration for experienced workers; its abstract is not a full methods review.
Individual generative-AI use, enterprise any-AI use, and task use have incompatible denominators. The sources are not independent measurements of one adoption rate.
No actual company data or deployment outcomes; organizational characteristics are assumptions.
confidence_and_uncertainty: Moderate confidence in broad, uneven US diffusion; low confidence in a precise Rogers stage or application/peer prevalence. Organizational timing is conditional inference with low-to-moderate confidence, not measured readiness.
value_opportunity_implication: Potential reduction in total service effort and support for less-experienced staff; no guaranteed 15% improvement or net cost saving for this organization.
risk_governance_implication: Human review, approved source content and escalation are case controls; their actual effectiveness must be tested. Quality and data risks can impede diffusion even when tools are widely available.
recommendation_management_implication: First evaluate generic bank service replies using approved content and controlled data. Resolve internal review and data-handling requirements before considering a live pilot; pass residual risk, costs and deployment authority to the Adoption Agent.
change_monitoring_triggers: New representative US application-specific adoption data distinguishing pilots and sustained deployment.
Measured local workflow effort, errors, repeat contacts and total costs from a bounded evaluation.
Changes in approved content, integration support, employee training or internal control readiness.
Refresh evidence before a six-month timing decision; no automatic launch date.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Abstain from a precise industry adoption rate or Rogers stage for human-reviewed service drafting. Need dated representative peer data with a clear denominator and production-use definition.
Do not claim the specific company will save 15%. Need comparable local inquiry tests including review, correction and tool costs.
Actual company peer position, data quality and integration capability remain unknown.
